Notes.Text:
This update for librsvg fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-96889: Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities (bsc#1282612).

Changes for librsvg:

- Update to version 2.57.5:
 + This is a security release for bug #1241, RUSTSEC-2026-0305 /
 CVE-2026-96889 / bsc#1282612:
 - glgo#GNOME/librsvg#1241: Fix use-after-free when there are
 duplicate XML entities in nested Xinclude documents. Thanks to
 Rafael B. Dias for reporting this in detail.
 - Dependency updates: lopdf for RUSTSEC-2026-0187, crossbeam-epoch for
 RUSTSEC-2026-0204, time for RUSTSEC-2026-0009.
 - The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is 1.89.0.

Vulnerabilities.Description: time provides date and time handling in Rust. From 0.3.6 to before 0.3.47, when user-provided input is provided to any type that parses with the RFC 2822 format, a denial of service attack via stack exhaustion is possible. The attack relies on formally deprecated and rarely-used features that are part of the RFC 2822 format used in a malicious manner. Ordinary, non-malicious input will never encounter this scenario. A limit to the depth of recursion was added in v0.3.47. From this version, an error will be returned rather than exhausting the stack.

Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in librsvg. When processing an SVG document containing nested XML inclusions (Xincludes) with duplicate entity declarations, a use-after-free error can occur. This vulnerability arises because the library incorrectly frees an XML entity that is still in use by the parser. An attacker could potentially exploit this to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code.
